The task: applicant axis conflict. Register says "Avery Berkel", document says "Avery Weigh-Tronix".

Background knowledge: Avery Berkel and Avery Weigh-Tronix are related companies — Avery Weigh-Tronix is the parent/brand (part of ITW), and Avery Berkel is a brand of weighing scales. In 2009, the company Avery Berkel was part of Avery Weigh-Tronix (ITW group). Historically, Avery Berkel Ltd was renamed; Avery Weigh-Tronix is the trading name of the company formerly known as Avery Berkel? Actually, let me think. Weigh-Tronix was a US company acquired by Avery Berkel? The history: GEC acquired Avery; Avery Berkel... In 2000, Avery Berkel was bought by Weigh-Tronix (US), forming Avery Weigh-Tronix. Later in 2010, Avery Weigh-Tronix... The company operated as "Avery Weigh-Tronix" with "Avery Berkel" as a brand for retail scales.

So in 2009, the applicant could legitimately be named either "Avery Berkel" (the brand/legacy name) or "Avery Weigh-Tronix" (the corporate entity). They are the same corporate entity trading under related names. The rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity". Are they genuinely different companies? They're closely related — Avery Berkel is a trading name of Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd. The register's OIML-CS database lists "Avery Berkel" while the certificate document says "Avery Weigh-Tronix".

Given the rules: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift = same-entity. These names are not spelling variants; they're distinct names but refer to the same corporate group/entity in practice. Hmm.

The intended answer likely: "same-entity" because Avery Berkel and Avery Weigh-Tronix are the same company (Avery Berkel is the brand; Avery Weigh-Tronix the corporate name) — best value should be... which one? Rules for same-entity don't explicitly say which value; for same-entity number format it says register's canonical form. For names, "same-entity" with best_value probably register's canonical form, or document's since certificate is legal instrument? The rules: different-entity → best_value = document's, since certificate is legal instrument. For same-entity, presumably register canonical form is fine, since it's the register canonical.

Actually the safest reading: same-entity → best_value = register's canonical form (register is canonical). The rule explicitly mentions register canonical for number formats; for names same-entity, using register form keeps consistency with the OIML-CS database.

Which verdict? I think "same-entity" is the intended verdict because Avery Berkel is the well-known brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix — the certificate issuer GB1 (NWML) issued to the same company. The register entry "Avery Berkel" and document "Avery Weigh-Tronix" both refer to the same corporate entity (Avery Berkel was renamed/rebranded Avery Weigh-Tronix around that era). So verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Avery Berkel" (register canonical) — or document's? Hmm.

If same-entity, which value should the fused record carry? The rules give guidance only for different-entity (document's) and same-entity numbers (register's canonical). For same-entity names, I'd default to the register's canonical form since it's a fused record anchored on the register id, and the document value is a rebrand/trading variant. Best value: "Avery Berkel".

Alternatively, one could argue "different-entity" since they're different names — but they're not "genuinely different company"; it's the same company under different trading names. The phrase "Genuinely different company or person names" implies truly distinct parties. Avery Berkel vs Avery Weigh-Tronix: Avery Weigh-Tronix is the parent company; Avery Berkel the brand. In OIML certificates context, applicant naming varied. I'll go same-entity.

Why sentence: "Avery Berkel is the trading brand of the same corporate entity as Avery Weigh-Tronix (shared heritage/brand relationship), so it's name drift, not a different applicant; keep the register's canonical form."
